Lesson 03: Investigating Erosion and Deposition (Grade 3, Explore Phase, 5E Model)

Learning Objective: Students will investigate the effects of water flow rate on erosion and
deposition of sand.

Performance Expectation: 3-ESS2-1. Represent data in tables and graphical displays to describe
typical weather conditions expected during a particular season.
DCI: ESS2.D — Weather and Climate
Focal SEP: Analyzing and Interpreting Data
Focal CCC: Cause and Effect

Timing: 50 minutes

Student-Facing Sequence:
1. Hook (5 min): Students view two photographs of a riverbank, one from ten years ago and one recent,
   and discuss with a partner what might have changed and why.
2. Investigation Setup (10 min): Groups build a stream table using a sand-filled tray tilted at a
   fixed angle, with a cup for controlled water pouring.
3. Trial 1 — Slow Pour (10 min): Students pour water slowly, observe where sand moves, and sketch the
   resulting pattern.
4. Trial 2 — Fast Pour (10 min): Students repeat with a faster pour rate, sketch the new pattern, and
   record observations in a data table comparing both trials.
5. Wrap-Up Discussion (15 min): Small groups compare their two trials and discuss which pour rate
   caused more erosion, then share one observation with the whole class.

Teacher Notes: Emphasize the vocabulary "erosion" and "deposition" during both trials. Ask "why"
follow-up questions after each trial to push beyond observation into explanation.

Vocabulary: erosion, deposition, sediment, flow rate.

Assessment Opportunity: Completed data table comparing slow vs. fast pour observations.

Existing Literacy Supports: None beyond the data table headers; there is no dedicated space for
students to explain their reasoning in writing.
